source.title: How to Choose the Right Relay Module for PLC Control Panels: A 7-Point Checklist
source.body:
Choosing a relay module looks simple until the panel is wired and the PLC output doesn’t match the coil voltage, or the contacts can’t carry the load. A few checks before ordering prevent most commissioning problems. If you’re new to the basics, first read our guide on[ what a relay module is and how it works in control panels](https://btc.net.in/what-is-a-relay-module-and-how-does-it-work-in-control-panels/), then use this checklist to narrow down the right unit.
Why Relay Module Selection Matters
A relay module sits between the controller and the field load. It lets a low-power PLC output switch contactor coils, solenoid valves, or lamps while keeping the control side electrically isolated. If the module is mismatched to the PLC or the load, you get unreliable switching, wasted DIN-rail space, or repeat site visits.
The 7-Point Checklist
1. Match the coil voltage to your PLC output.
 This is the first check. Connectwell’s slim electromechanical modules cover 5V, 12V, 24V, 48-60V, 120V, and 230V, while the CRM series spans 12V DC up to 220V DC/AC. Choosing the right voltage avoids extra adapters.
2. Count the contacts you need.
 Modules come in 1, 2, or 4 changeover (CO) configurations. Pick based on how many independent circuits each channel must switch.
3. Check the contact current rating.
 CRM series contacts are rated from roughly 5A to 12A. For heavier loads, let the relay drive a contactor instead of switching the load directly.
4. Choose the terminal type.
 Screw clamp suits most standard panels. Spring clamp is faster to wire and holds up better where terminals are reworked often.
5. Decide between pluggable and soldered.
 Pluggable relays can be swapped in the field without rewiring. Soldered versions give a more permanent, vibration-resistant connection.
6. Pick electromechanical or solid state (SSR).
 For frequent switching, where contact wear and switching noise matter, slim solid-state modules are the better fit.
7. Plan for diagnostics.
 An LED status indicator and a manual test or override button make commissioning and fault-finding much quicker.
Which Series Suits Which Panel?
Standard automation and control panels: CRM and CRL modular relays with base
Many outputs in a small space: CIMRE relay interface boards (2, 4, or 8 channel, IP20 enclosed)
Tight DIN-rail space: slim relay modules
Standalone plug-in relays: CW modular relay sockets (1 CO, 2 CO, 4 CO)
You can compare all of these in BTC’s relay module range or go straight to the Connectwell relay modules.
Build the Whole DIN Rail Together
Relay modules rarely work alone. They sit beside terminal blocks and other[ Connectwell panel accessories](https://btc.net.in/product-category/panel-accessory/connectwell-panel-accessory/), so sourcing them together keeps your bill of materials with one supplier and your parts compatible.
Where These Modules Are Used
Relay modules are standard in automation and process control panels, power transmission and distribution systems, and[ OEM machine-building](https://btc.net.in/oems-original-equipment-manufacturers/) applications.
